h1:
China Lighting Sourcing
Pendant, Table & Architectural Fixtures
lead: Lighting sits between a design object and an electrical product, and it is regulated as the second one. Wiring, drivers, earthing and certification decide whether a fixture can legally be installed in your market, and none of that is visible in a photograph. We buy lighting out of the Zhongshan and Guzhen belt, and we confirm the electrical specification and the documents before a fixture is ordered in volume.
sub_intro: Most lighting orders mix decorative pieces for visible areas with functional fixtures for everything else. Both come from the same supplier network.

subcategories.name: Pendant Lights
subcategories.desc: Single pendants, cluster pendants and large statement fixtures for dining tables, stairwells and reception areas.

subcategories.name: Table & Floor Lamps
subcategories.desc: Bedside lamps, reading lamps, floor lamps and task lighting in ceramic, glass, metal and fabric.

subcategories.name: Ceiling & Flush Mounts
subcategories.desc: Flush and semi-flush ceiling lights, downlights and surface-mounted fixtures for circulation areas.

subcategories.name: Wall Sconces
subcategories.desc: Interior and exterior wall lights, bathroom sconces and up-down wall washers, hard-wired or plug-in.

subcategories.name: Architectural & Linear
subcategories.desc: Linear profiles, track systems, cove lighting and bespoke architectural fixtures built to a drawing.

subcategories.name: Outdoor & Landscape
subcategories.desc: Path lights, bollards, spike lights, garden lanterns and IP-rated exterior fixtures.

mat_intro: With lighting, the shade material is the easy half. The electrical half — driver, earthing, ingress rating — is what determines whether the fixture passes inspection at your end.

materials.name: Metal
materials.note: Brass, steel, aluminium and stainless, in plated, brushed, powder-coated or hand-patinated finishes. Ask for coating thickness on anything going into a bathroom or coastal property.

materials.name: Glass
materials.note: Mouth-blown, opal, frosted, ribbed and clear glass. Fragile and heavy; the packing spec matters as much as the product.

materials.name: Fabric & paper shades
materials.note: Linen, cotton and paper shades, often hand-assembled. Check the lining and whether the shade is fire-treated for your market.

materials.name: Rattan, cane & wood
materials.note: Woven and timber shades that read warm and natural. Batch variation is normal, so approve a physical sample.

materials.name: Crystal & acrylic
materials.note: Machine-cut crystal and acrylic for chandeliers and decorative pieces. Confirm whether it is leaded crystal or acrylic, which changes both weight and documentation.

materials.name: LED & electrical components
materials.note: Integrated LED, external drivers, dimming compatibility and colour temperature. Confirm CRI, kelvin, dimming protocol and whether the driver is replaceable.

buy_intro: Lighting is quoted on specification. These are the ranges buyers plan around before the electrical details are confirmed.

buying.label: Typical MOQ
buying.note: Stocked decorative fixtures often start at two to ten pieces. Custom finishes, sizes or architectural runs usually begin at twenty to fifty units.

buying.label: Lead time
buying.note: Ten to twenty-five days for stocked items; thirty to fifty days for made-to-order or finished-to-sample work.

buying.label: Sampling
buying.note: One sample fixture is worth buying. It settles finish, colour temperature and build quality faster than any specification sheet.

buying.label: Packaging
buying.note: Shades packed separately from frames, with inner boxes and corner protection. Glass and crystal get dedicated crating at volume.

buying.label: Compliance
buying.note: CE and UKCA for Europe and the UK, UL or ETL for North America, SAA for Australia, plus RoHS and the correct voltage for your market.

buy_footnote: Confirm the certification your market requires before ordering, not after. A fixture without the right mark cannot be installed legally, however good it looks.
check_intro: Lighting quotes are only accurate once the electrical environment is known.

faq_intro: These are the questions that decide whether a lighting order can be installed without surprises.

faq.q: What certification do your lights carry?
faq.a: It depends on what your market requires and what the factory holds. Common marks are CE and UKCA for Europe and the UK, UL or ETL for North America, and SAA for Australia, alongside RoHS. Tell us the installation country and we will confirm which marks the fixture can actually be supplied with, rather than quoting a generic claim.

faq.q: Can you supply the right voltage for my country?
faq.a: Yes. Voltage is specified at the time of order, typically 110–120V at 60Hz for North America and 220–240V at 50Hz elsewhere. Integrated LED fixtures may also need a driver rated for your supply, which we confirm with the factory before production rather than after it.

Only if specified that way. Dimmability depends on both the driver and the dimmer type in your building, so we ask which dimming protocol is already installed before quoting. Retrofitting a driver after installation costs far more than choosing the right one up front.

faq.q: Can you make a fixture from a drawing?
faq.a: Yes. Architectural and custom decorative fixtures are regularly built to a drawing or a reference photograph, with a sample made first for approval. Bespoke work generally starts at twenty to fifty units and takes longer than a stocked item, so it suits projects with a fixed schedule.
